title: Telangana
name: Telangana
intro: Telangana gained twelve assembly seats in the 2008 delimitation, rising from 107 to 119, six years before it became a state. The order also renumbered it first: in the undivided Andhra Pradesh of 1976 the Telangana seats ran from 188 to 294, and in the 2008 order they run from 1 to 119. What is shown here is the Telangana portion of each map.

map_caveats: Both maps predate the division of Andhra Pradesh. The 1976 order drew 294 assembly constituencies for the undivided state and the 2008 order redrew all 294; the state was divided only in June 2014, and no fresh delimitation has followed. The maps here are the Telangana portion of each order, and the seats shown are exactly those that fell to Telangana on division.

Territory lineage is given on two footings, and each seat record states which applies to it. For 93 of the 107 pre-2008 seats the link is derived from the text of the 1976 and 2008 orders. The 1976 order describes constituencies in taluks and firkas and the 2008 order in mandals, which were carved out of those taluks in 1985 and largely kept their names; where the names correspond the link is textual. For the remainder the successor shown is the one holding the largest share of the old seat's area, inferred from the boundaries alone.

The pre-2008 boundaries have been georectified. The source digitisation of the 1976-order map was displaced about four and a half kilometres north relative to the 2008-order map. The correction was fitted on the outer boundary of the undivided state and raises the agreement between the two outlines from an intersection-over-union of 0.95 to 0.97; tested against the constituencies that kept their names, none of which was used to fit it, average overlap rises from 53 to 59 per cent.
Seat numbers on the pre-2008 side are those of the undivided state, which is why the pre-2008 seats run from 188 to 294, the numbers under which they were actually contested.
Territory percentages are measured from the mapped boundaries in every case, and are areal shares, not shares of the electorate.
footnotes: Andhra Pradesh was divided on 2 June 2014. The 2008 order's constituencies numbered 1 to 119 passed to Telangana and those numbered 120 to 294 remained with Andhra Pradesh; neither set was redrawn on division.
Reservation status reflects the category in force at the time of the relevant order, not any later reclassification.
